findings.title: Job 'close_cycle' started and never finished
findings.summary: 'close_cycle' started on nng_repro[1] at 4274.86 ms and had not finished 1170.04 ms later, until the end of the trace (budget 500.00 ms). The process's threads were blocked: nng_repro[1] CONDVAR on 0x0000003088e0b8e8; nng_repro[3] REPLY; nng_repro[4] CONDVAR on 0x00000022fe3bf6f0; nng_repro[5] CONDVAR on 0x00000022fe3bf6f0; nng_repro[6] CONDVAR on 0x00000022fe3bf6f0; nng_repro[7] CONDVAR on 0x00000022fe3bf6f0; nng_repro[8] CONDVAR on 0x0000001dfcb50de0; nng_repro[9] CONDVAR on 0x0000001dfcb50de0.

findings.title: Unusual behaviour in nng_repro[3]
findings.summary: nng_repro[3] (prio 10) behaved unlike healthy QNX programs in 54 of its 55 time windows; the most unusual stretch lasted 980 ms. It stands out in: how often it blocks (higher than healthy), CPU migrations (higher than healthy), how often it is preempted (higher than healthy). The closest pattern TraceLens has seen is two processes blocked sending to each other, but only loosely (distance 17.37 against 0.906 typical for it): treat this as behaviour of its own.
findings.qnx_note: Learned from healthy QNX 8.0 traces: this thread behaved unlike any healthy run in the features listed. It is not a proven bug and gets no automatic fix: look at the timeline around it. Any resemblance to a known pattern is measured against labelled example windows, never a rule that fired.
